message.content:
Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that normally takes **about 12 weeks (roughly three months)**.  

Here’s why:

| Factor | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Surface area** | Roughly 10 000 m² of exposed metal (the exact figure varies by source, but it’s on the order of ten thousand square‑metres). |
| **Work schedule** | The tower is repainted every 7 years. Each repaint is carried out in stages, with scaffolding, safety nets, and protective equipment set up around the structure. |
| **Crew size** | Around 300–400 painters and support staff work on the project, often in shifts to cover all angles of the tower. |
| **Coats applied** | Typically two or three coats of paint are applied, with drying time between layers. |
| **Time per coat** | About 4–5 weeks per coat, including preparation, application, and curing. |

So, from start to finish—preparation, primer, first coat, second coat, final inspection—the whole process usually spans **12 weeks**. This aligns with the official maintenance schedule maintained by the Société d’Exploitation de la Tour Eiffel (SETE), which manages the tower’s upkeep.
